name: Monounsaturated fat
what_is:
Monounsaturated fats have a single double bond in their chain. The most common is oleic acid, the one that predominates in olive oil.

They are also abundant in avocado, nuts, rapeseed oil and high-oleic sunflower oil.

On a nutrition label they are a voluntary field in almost every market. The European Union permits declaring them but does not require it, so most products do not show them.

Where they appear, they sit inside the total fat figure, not alongside it.
why_botia:
BOTIA flags monounsaturated fat because when it is declared it explains much of a product's composition, and because its absence misleads.

A label not declaring them does not mean the product has none. It means that market does not require the declaration.
can_1: Read the declared value, where it exists, and keep its unit and its basis.
can_2: State that they form part of the total fat figure and are not added to it.
can_3: Link to the oils and ingredients in the list that provide them, where they can be identified.
cannot_1: Work them out by subtracting saturated and polyunsaturated from the total. That subtraction does not give monounsaturated: the total also includes trans fats and, depending on the method, other components.
cannot_2: Treat an undeclared value as zero. It is a voluntary field in almost every market.
cannot_3: Say how much is oleic acid and how much other monounsaturated acids. The label declares the group, not its composition.
